newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIAN BROADCASTING CORP MORNING UPDATE.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIAN BROADCASTING CORP MORNING UPDATE.

text.p: BORBIDGE CONFIDENT OF CUNNINGHAM'S SUPPORT
Queensland Premier Rob Borbidge is confident Gladstone Independent Liz Cunningham will not support Opposition moves to unseat his Government when Parliament resumes next week.

Ms Cunningham met Attorney General Denver Beanland yesterday for a briefing on his plans to introduce legislation overhauling the Criminal Justice Commission after the Supreme Court scuttled the Connolly-Ryan Inquiry.
Mr Beanland has refused to comment except to say the meeting was "convivial and harmonious".
Mr Borbidge said he had no reason to believe Mrs Cunningham would deviate from her previous commitment to vote with the Government on matters of supply and confidence, unless corruption was involved.
BISHOP TAKES A DIVE - IN A SUBMARINE
Defence Industry Minister Bronwyn Bishop will today submerge - and stay for a night - in one of the Navy's new Collins-class submarines.
A Navy representative said the Minister would board the Farncomb, near Thistle Island, for exercises in Spencer Gulf.
She will be accompanied by the Australian Submarine Corporation's managing director, Hans Ohff, and the Navy's director-general of planning and policy, Commodore Mick Dunne.
Farncomb is the second of six submarines being built in Adelaide for the Navy.
CABINET COULD SEE NEW PROPOSAL ON MEDIA LAWS TODAY
Prime Minister John Howard has been urged to ensure Cabinet will not make any decision on changes to media ownership rules until Coalition MPs are consulted.
Communications Minister Richard Alston may put a proposal to change media laws to Cabinet as early as today.
Senator Alston is understood to back a relaxation of cross media ownership rules, with a public inquiry for proprietors to justify their bids before final approval is given to any changes.
The Coalition's communications committee has written to Mr Howard, asking him to honour a commitment to consult the backbench before Cabinet makes a decision.
Committee secretary Gary Hardgrave said a public inquiry was a good idea.
He said media owners should welcome the chance to argue their case in public and said it would also honour a Coalition promise that decisions on media laws would be open and accountable.
COSTELLO WELCOMES MOVE TO REFUND FRANCHISE FEES
Federal Treasurer, Peter Costello, says he welcomes moves by the States who have agreed to refund pre-paid franchise fees.
The Commonwealth has offered to collect petrol, liquor and tobacco taxes previously levied by the states, worth $5 billion, which the High Court has ruled as unconstitutional.
Mr Costello has urged States and Territories to reimburse all pre-paid licence fees, so they do not engage in double dipping and so consumers are not hit with any price rises.
New South Wales and Victoria have shifted ground, agreeing to repay a portion of the licensing fees.
